items.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has justified Kyiv's repeated attacks on a critical bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, calling it a "fair response" to 109 separate Russian attacks on bridges in Ukraine. In comments to the BBC in Kyiv, Zelensky said the intense attacks on Ukraine by Russia that have followed the strikes on the Crimean Bridge were only a "signal that Vladimir Putin does not want to stop. He wants a reason to escalate". He rejected the claim by the Russian president that the bridge - which links Russia to the peninsula it illegally annexed from Ukraine - was "exclusively civilian" in use. "There are facts, not just the words of Putin. We can see," he said. The Ukrainian president pointed to images online of tanks and other Russian military hardware using the route from Russia into occupied Crimea as a supply line and for logistics. The Ukrainian president added that Russia had carried out attacks with missiles and drones on bridges in Ukraine. items.blurb: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities.
items.text: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10–18ft are expected, with local sets of 18–22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. items.headline: Russia-bound ship attacked in Gulf of Finland
items.blurb: Finnish defence forces say that Ukraine was likely behind the drone attack on the vessel.
items.text: A Russian cargo vessel bound for the country's Baltic exclave Kaliningrad has been hit by a drone attack in the eastern Gulf of Finland, Russian and Finnish authorities say. The ship - the Sparta II - caught on fire after the strike on Saturday morning, before drifting into Finnish waters. Finnish defence forces said Ukraine was likely behind the attack. Kyiv has yet to comment. "War is spilling over into our immediate vicinity," Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said. "Ukraine has the right to fight back against the aggressor." Kaliningrad Governor Alexei Besprozvannykh said two drones had been used, based on preliminary information, and there was "no threat" to the territory's supplies. The Sparta II was sanctioned by the US in 2022 and Ukraine earlier this year, and is run by a Russian company, according to the Ukrainian and US governments. The company says on its website that it was established within the structure of Russia's defence ministry in 2011 and since 2015 has been operating within the military construction complex. items.blurb: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.
items.text: The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia. The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa , on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions. The department of forestry, fisheries and the environment confirmed the trees had been destined for Georgia but did not name the buyer. The case echoes an episode in Kenya four years ago , when eight baobabs were uprooted to be exported to Shekvetili Dendrological Park , owned by Bidzina Ivanishvili, an influential Georgian billionaire and the country’s former prime minister. items.headline: Fight over fossil fuels leaves COP31 climate talks in deadlock
items.blurb: Countries from nearly 200 countries are in a deadlock to try and get a new global climate agreement.
items.text: Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock and have been suspended for the night, after running more than a day over time, as countries have been unable to agree on a new global climate deal. The EU and Pacific island nations are amongst a group pushing back against the latest draft agreement which included no reference to reducing the world's demand for fossil fuels. A second sticking point involves a push from the Africa Group to get commitments on more money for adaptation - but the EU has previously said it would not support this. Negotiating teams due to fly out on Sunday morning are now moving their flights to Monday in a sign that a deal is not yet in sight. If countries cannot reach consensus - which is required by the UN's climate talks process - the negotiations could be suspended. In that case the summit would end with no deal and be reconvened next year. This has only happened once before since countries started holding COP climate meetings in 1995. On Saturday,

items.headline: Lebanese president demands Israel withdrawal, decries Iran’s interference
items.blurb: Joseph Aoun says 'two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked' mean Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence.
items.text: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun has decried Iran’s meddling in Lebanon’s affairs and demanded Israel’s withdrawal from his country’s south. In a speech on Saturday, on the eve of Lebanon’s 83rd independence anniversary, Aoun said Lebanon faces two interconnected fateful tests: the “Israeli occupation of parts of our land” and “foreign interference” from “some influential parties in the Iranian regime” through weapons and decisions outside the authority of the Lebanese state. These “two fundamental obstacles, inseparably linked” mean that Lebanon cannot fully celebrate its independence, he added. “Withdraw from every inch of Lebanese territory. Stop your attacks. And return our captives,” Aoun demanded of Israel. Dozens of Lebanese citizens are believed to be held in Israeli detention centres , including civilians as well as members of the Hezbollah armed group captured during fighting in southern Lebanon. items.blurb: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.
items.text: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report. In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund ( UNFPA ) published on Thursday. Younger women and girls aged 15 to 19 had even less power to say no, compared with older women aged 45 to 49, according to analysis in the report of eight countries with comparable data (Angola, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kazakhstan, Malawi, Mali, Nigeria, Tajikistan and Zambia). items.blurb: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Idisro" Meza Flores, who is accused of drug trafficking and torture, is detained after gun fight with authorities.
items.text: A Mexican drug lord who was on the FBI's 10 most wanted list has been arrested following a shoot-out with Mexican authorities. Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores and seven others were detained by Mexican special forces in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, Mexico's defence secretariat said. Seven suspects were killed in the operation, as were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave, the secretariat added. Meza Flores was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, while he has been accused of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs" by the FBI. The US is seeking his extradition. Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump since he returned to the White House. Meza Flores, the leader of the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, is thought to have been active in the drug trafficking trade since the 1990s but managed to evade authorities till now by maintaining a relatively low profile. items.text: The Criminal Investigation Department ( CID ) of West Bengal has taken over the investigation into a case involving alleged impersonation of Minister Kshudiram Tudu to influence the ongoing recruitment process of the Staff Selection Commission (SSC), officials said on Saturday. The accused, identified as Zulfiqar Ali, was arrested by Bidhannagar Police from Deganga following a complaint lodged by the SSC Secretary at Bidhannagar East Police Station. He further said that the SSC Secretary submitted a written complaint, following which the police arrested the accused. "He submitted a written complaint, following which the Bidhan Nagar Police arrested a person identified as Zulfiqar Ali, a resident of Devdanga. The CID took over the case today, and the investigation is currently underway," he added. The CID chief said further details would be shared as the investigation progresses. Earlier, in a separate case on September 15, the Jharkhand CID arrested two accused in separate cases related to alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, officials said. items.blurb: Addressing a press conference in Dehradun, party’s state president Uma Sisodia said that there have been “no positive developments” regarding an alliance.
items.text: The Aam Aadmi Party ( AAP ) on Saturday announced it will contest all 70 assembly seats in the forthcoming Uttarakhand elections scheduled next year, ruling out any immediate possibility of a pre-election tie up. Addressing a press conference in Dehradun, party’s state president Uma Sisodia said that there have been “no positive developments” regarding an alliance with any party so far, and the leadership has decided to go solo following consultations with national convener Arvind Kejriwal. “The entire state executive, district units, and all assembly presidents held detailed discussions with Kejriwal and the high command to review preparations for the upcoming assembly elections. It has been decided that we will strongly contest all 70 seats.”

items.text: Medical experts say that the use of fairness creams containing heavy metals such as mercury to lighten the skin is emerging as a major health hazard that can lead to serious conditions such as kidney failure if not diagnosed early. Illustration: Soumyadip Sinha. The craze for fairness is more than skin-deep, and the trade-off can be costly. Inferior cosmetic products can end up harming your vital organs. A 17-year-old girl in Keralam’s Malappuram developed a serious kidney ailment allegedly after using a fairness cream purchased online following its promotion by social media influencers, according to the doctors treating her. The incident came to light after the authorities at the hospital that treated the teenager, who was diagnosed with membranous nephropathy, held a press conference on Friday. Lab tests had confirmed 1.25% mercury in the cosmetic product, according to the hospital sources. items.text: The Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers' Union, popularly known as Gokul Milk Union, has decided to increase the selling price of buffalo milk by ₹6 per litre and cow milk by ₹4 per litre with immediate effect, its chairman Rajesh Patil said on Saturday. The decision was taken unanimously by all 25 directors due to the drought situation and the difficulties faced by farmers, Patil, a former MLA, said. The union has also decided to raise the procurement rates paid to milk producers by ₹3 per litre for buffalo milk and ₹2 per litre for cow milk, he said, adding that this hike was "historic". "The revised rates will come into effect from November 21 and remain applicable for around 131 days, till March. The situation will be reviewed every month, and the board will take further decisions depending on the circumstances," Patil said. He said milk availability was likely to decline significantly across Maharashtra, including Kolhapur district, and the union would have to take decisions accordingly. items.headline: Paolo Bulgari, the Italian jeweler who turned a family business into global luxury brand, dies at 89
items.blurb: Paolo Bulgari, the Italian jeweler who turned a family business into global luxury brand, dies at 89
items.text: ATHENS, Greece (AP) — Paolo Bulgari, the grandson of a Greek silversmith who helped transform the family jewelry business into a global luxury brand synonymous with Italian glamour and design, has died. He was 89. His family announced his death Saturday, describing him as “the greatest jeweler of our time” and praising his humanity and entrepreneurial talent. Bulgari presided for decades over a brand celebrated by supermodels, Hollywood stars and collectors for its bold designs and distinctive use of color. Born in Rome in 1937, he was the grandson of Sotirios Voulgaris, who founded the jewelry business after leaving Greece. Originally from Paramythia, a mountain village in the Epirus region of northwestern Greece renowned for its silver jewelry, Voulgaris fled Ottoman rule and settled in Naples before opening a shop in Rome, adapting both his craft and his family name to his new home. Paolo Bulgari joined the family business shortly after leaving school. Working alongside his father, Giorgio, he initially focused on precious stones, developing an expertise in gemstones that would inform his work as a designer and businessman

Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on users’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.” “Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she said. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.” Signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS. items.text: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. items.text: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These “AI routers,” sometimes also known as “AI gateways,” receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task. Instead of using Anthropic, OpenAI, or another big provider, the developer hires an AI router to find the most suitable model. items.text: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.” “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.” In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating

items.headline: Chips can survive the space environment — can their financing?
items.blurb: Lenders don't want SpaceX shooting their collateral into orbit. What does that mean for space data centers writ large?
items.text: The push to build data centers in space faces plenty of obstacles, from tricky engineering to a dearth of rockets that could take chips to orbit. But what about paying for the chips? The data center ecosystem currently depends on debt financing, with cloud providers borrowing to build out data centers and then paying back the loans with a share of the revenue. Those deals typically use the chips as collateral — if the data centers default on their loans, the lenders can take possession of the chips and resell them. That backstop makes it cheaper for companies to finance their chips. Even older chips retain value — according to Compute Credit Index Research , some H100s are selling for about half of their original cost basis from 2023, while some H200 configurations are selling for the same price they did when introduced in 2024. But you’re not going to repossess chips installed in a satellite orbiting 300 miles above Earth at 17,500 miles per hour. items.blurb: Sarvam AI’s latest announcement of its Token Factory has brought a new layer of India’s artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure ecosystem…
items.text: Sarvam AI's Token Factory launch has brought India's emerging inference-as-a-service market into focus, with L&T, E2E Networks' Jarvislabs, Utho Labs and Mirror Security also building offerings around token-based AI infrastructure. Token factories allow developers and enterprises to access multiple AI models through APIs and pay for the tokens they consume, without having to manage GPU infrastructure or model deployment themselves. As AI adoption drives demand for inference, Indian infrastructure players are looking to move beyond GPU rentals and monetise computing capacity through managed services, with an opportunity to serve both domestic and global workloads. Sarvam AI’s latest announcement of its Token Factory has brought a new layer of India’s artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure ecosystem into focus. The Bengaluru-based startup on November 16 launched a commercial platform that allows developers and enterprises to access multiple AI models through its computing infrastructure. The launch comes as Indian companies look to capitalise on the growing demand for AI inference, the process through which trained models generate responses to user prompts. items.headline: Scaler Cofounder Anshuman Singh Unveils AI Training Data Venture Arcfront
items.blurb: Tech upskilling platform Scaler’s cofounder Anshuman Singh has unveiled Arcfront, an AI research and training data venture that turns records…
items.text: Scaler cofounder Anshuman Singh has unveiled Arcfront with Naman Bhalla, claiming four of the five frontier AI labs became customers within a year. Arcfront is commercialising records of expert decision-making to help AI developers train and test models on professional tasks that require judgement beyond producing correct answers. Arcfront operates under Evaratus Inc., with company recruitment material identifying Evaratus as formerly Scaler AI Labs. Its current ownership relationship with Scaler remains unconfirmed. Tech upskilling platform Scaler’s cofounder Anshuman Singh has unveiled Arcfront, an AI research and training data venture that turns records of how professionals solve problems into material for training and testing advanced AI models. Singh is building the venture with Naman Bhalla, Scaler’s former head of AI products and an ex-Google software engineer. In a post on X, Singh said Arcfront also has “deep support” from Scaler cofounder Abhimanyu Saxena. Singh claimed that four of the five frontier AI labs became Arcfront’s customers within less than a year of operations. However, he did not identify the labs. Arcfront operates under Evaratus Inc., according to its website’s legal disclosures.
